text:
Zoe: hey all — new hire morning. trying to follow the mac M1 bootstrap but hitting weirdness: i installed brew under /opt/homebrew, asdf is in my dotfiles, but some formulas (old node, some kafka tools) only exist as Intel bottles and brew wants me to run under rosetta. when i try `arch -x86_64 brew install node@14` it installs but node binary is under /usr/local and my asdf build later picks up arm bottles. super confusing. anyone maintain a simple pattern for rossetta-only formulas?

Alex: welcome Zoe! :wave: short answer: keep arm brew as default (/opt/homebrew) and use a separate intel brew prefix for Rosetta-only stuff. we have a mini-guide in devex: install the Intel brew under /usr/local with `arch -x86_64 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"` then use `arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/brew install <formula>` for intel bottles. add the intel brew bin to PATH only in a terminal where you need it, e.g., `alias intel-brew='arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/brew'`.

Zoe: ok that helps. next the asdf python i built earlier seems to link against arm openssl and a few node native modules fail in CI that runs under linux-gnu (we pin asdf/.tool-versions). is the recommended approach to build everything natively on each arch and commit the .tool-versions only?

Priya: yes commit `.tool-versions` only. builds should be native per-host. if you need deterministic binaries across arch (rare) use containerized builds in CI. also watch out for PATH order — ensure `/opt/homebrew/bin` (arm) is first on arm machines, and `/usr/local/bin` (intel) is first in rosetta shells.

Zoe: got it. a separate issue: our corp proxy injects a custom CA and i started getting `SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` errors when pip/requests hit internal package indexes. i added the CA to keychain but python still fails. any env var fixes?

Alex: yes, on mac python doesn't read the macOS keychain CA by default. set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to point to the PEM bundle with your company CA, e.g.:
```
export SSL_CERT_FILE="$HOME/.config/certs/corp-ca.pem"
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE="$HOME/.config/certs/corp-ca.pem"
```
we keep a small script `devex/add-corp-ca.sh` that exports those and copies the PEM from the corporate vault. don't commit the PEM — store in 1Password and fetch in your bootstrap.

Zoe: sweet — i pulled the PEM from 1Password and set the env vars, pip works now. another awkward bit: my dotfiles symlink `~/.gitconfig` to `~/dotfiles/git/config` but vscode when launched from the dock doesn't pick up my GPG signing settings (no `user.signingkey`). launching code from terminal works. is this the usual GUI env issue?

Priya: yep. GUI apps launched from the Dock/Spotlight don't inherit your shell env. two fixes: 1) put essential git config entries in `~/.gitconfig` (not just symlinked to a path that expects direnv), or 2) launch VS Code from terminal while you fix env propagation. also ensure `gpg-agent` socket is accessible to GUI apps; we recommend using the native macOS GPG tools or 1Password agent for GUI workflows.

Zoe: last small things: pre-commit hooks failing with `black` not found in CI lint job; i think the job uses system python. any quick CI tip?

Alex: ensure your CI step uses `.tool-versions` or install the right python version in the CI image. alternatively configure pre-commit to install language-specific venvs (use `language: python` in hooks) so it self-manages. we also pin pre-commit versions in devex config.

Zoe: answered everything — i added a `SETUP.M1.md` to dotfiles describing intel-brew pattern, SSL_CERT_FILE, and the VS Code GUI caveats. thanks y'all! :tada:

Devex Bot: Nice work, Zoe — checklist reminder: 1) commit `asdf/.tool-versions`, 2) keep arm/intel brew separate (don't mix PATHs), 3) store corp CA in 1Password and set `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, 4) direnv + 1Password for secrets, 5) launch GUI apps from terminal when testing env vars. Full docs: https://redwood.ai/devex/bootstrap and open a PR to `github.com/redwood-onboarding/dotfiles` for review.
